H. Res. 1

 In the House of Representatives, U. S.,

 January 3, 2025.
 Resolved, That Kevin McCumber of the State of Illinois be, and is hereby, 
chosen Clerk of the House of Representatives.
 Resolved, That William McFarland of the State of Maryland be, and is hereby, 
chosen Sergeant-at-Arms of the House of Representatives.
 Resolved, That Catherine Szpindor of the Commonwealth of Virginia be, and is 
hereby, chosen Chief Administrative Officer of the House of Representatives.

CHIPS and Science Act of 2022

SECTION 101. SEMICONDUCTOR INCENTIVES.

(a) FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM.—The Secretary of Commerce shall establish in the Department of Commerce a program to provide Federal financial assistance to covered entities to incentivize investment in facilities and equipment in the United States for semiconductor fabrication, assembly, testing, advanced packaging, production, or research and development.

(b) AMOUNT.—The Secretary may provide Federal financial assistance to a covered entity under this section in an aggregate amount of not more than $3,000,000,000 for any individual project.

(c) NATIONAL SEMICONDUCTOR TECHNOLOGY CENTER.—The Secretary of Commerce, in collaboration with the Secretary of Defense and the Director of the National Science Foundation, shall establish a National Semiconductor Technology Center to conduct research and prototyping of advanced semiconductor technology.

(d) NATIONAL SECURITY GUARDRAILS.—As a condition of receiving Federal financial assistance under this section, a covered entity shall agree that, for a period of 10 years, the entity will not engage in any significant transaction involving the material expansion of semiconductor manufacturing capacity in the People's Republic of China or any other foreign country of concern.

Sponsor: Rep. Frank D. Lucas [R-OK-3]. Cosponsors: 28 bipartisan members including Rep. Eddie Bernice Johnson [D-TX-30].

Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act

SECTION 11401. HIGHWAY SAFETY IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM.

(a) SAFE SYSTEM APPROACH.—The Administrator of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, in consultation with the Administrator of the Federal Highway Administration, shall develop a comprehensive strategy incorporating the Safe System approach to reduce fatalities and serious injuries on the Nation's highways.

(b) VULNERABLE ROAD USER SAFETY ASSESSMENT.—Each State shall complete a vulnerable road user safety assessment as part of its Strategic Highway Safety Plan under section 148(d) of title 23, United States Code. The assessment shall include:
(1) a quantitative analysis of vulnerable road user fatalities and serious injuries, including pedestrians, bicyclists, and motorcyclists;
(2) identification of high-risk corridors based on crash data from the Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) maintained by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration;
(3) strategies to address infrastructure, behavioral, and speed management factors.

(c) FUNDING.—Of the amounts made available under section 11101(a)(1), the Secretary of Transportation shall set aside $5,000,000,000 for the Safe Streets and Roads for All grant program administered by the Federal Highway Administration.

Sponsor: Sen. Tom Carper [D-DE]. Chair, Senate Environment and Public Works Committee. Cosponsors include Sen. Shelley Moore Capito [R-WV] and Sen. Ben Cardin [D-MD].
